skill.displayName: Pet Picky Eater Detection | 宠物选择性拒食识别

llm.summary: This skill appears to do more than pet feeding analysis, including remote video processing, identity/credential handling, history storage, and mismatched human health/face-analysis behavior that needs review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is picky-eater or pet feeding-bowl video analysis, but the referenced API documentation and rendering paths include human face, constitution, organ-condition, and health-warning analysis fields, which is a material purpose mismatch.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions reportedly require an open-id for history and direct the agent to read local configuration/API-key material as an identifier, which is not proportionate to ordinary video analysis.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No separate hidden installer or startup persistence was evidenced, but the package includes shared service modules and broader API wrappers whose capabilities exceed the advertised single analysis workflow.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Sending local videos or remote video URLs to a backend is expected for server-side analysis, but the artifacts do not clearly disclose privacy, retention, or the additional identity/auth metadata sent with requests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifacts indicate saved media/history, token persistence, report listing, and exposed add/edit/delete-style API operations, including destructive record changes without clear user confirmation or scope controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending feeding-area videos or URLs to the publisher’s remote service and sharing an identifier tied to analysis history. Before use, confirm the service is actually pet-feeding focused, does not process human biometric or health data, does not reuse API keys as user IDs, and provides clear deletion, retention, and authorization controls.
llm.findings:
[SSD-3] unexpected: Accepted as material: using an API key or local config credential as a user open-id is not necessary for pet video analysis and creates credential/identity confusion.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in context: broad record-management and report-listing capabilities are not clearly disclosed by the advertised analysis-only purpose.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: account provisioning, token storage, local config reads, and delete/edit operations are high-impact behaviors that need explicit scoping and user control.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted as material: face/health/constitution result fields contradict the pet feeding use case and could expose sensitive human-analysis data in the wrong workflow.
[SQP-2] expected: Partly expected for remote media analysis, but still a review concern because upload, local saving, identifier collection, and deletion behavior lack clear consent, retention, and confirmation safeguards.
